messages.author: f54103ce6753d56c
messages.subject: qplot boxplot and ylim
parts:
Hi
I am a newbie to R and am trying to use qplot to generate boxplots.  I am trying to use ylim to set a common display scale for multiple plots.  However, when I use that the box plot I get is different.  Does ylim also restrict the data that is used to create the boxplot or is it only to change the visual display of the axis?

Here is an example:
x <- rep("Dec",6)
y <- c(3,2.3,3.1,16,16.5,20)
d <- data.frame(x,y)
qplot(x,y,data=d,geom="boxplot")
qplot(x,y,data=d,geom="boxplot",ylim=c(0,8))

messages.author: dd68a26ecdacedb8
messages.subject: Re: qplot boxplot and ylim
parts:
I don't know the function well enough to explain the behaviour but am replying with a tip that is helpful in situations like this. I'm also adding an example.

A good practice is to use the max() of your measure for the upper limit on the scale:

x <- rep("Dec",6)
y <- c(3, 2.3, 3.1, 16, 16.5, 20)
d <- data.frame(x,y)

qplot(x,y,data=d, geom="boxplot", ylim=c(0,max(y)))

I'm hoping that a more knowledgeable member of the group can answer your question and explain the design decisions. To spur conversation, I've attached an example of a Cleveland plot of the count of flights for each day of the week (from the airline on-time statistics dataset). This plot shows the same behaviour as the plot that you included. Here, I set upper limit to 90,000. The values for days Monday and Sunday exceed 90,000 and the marks are not plotted.

-Phil

messages.author: 5a37f1244321fb07
messages.subject: RE: qplot boxplot and ylim
parts:
If you want to set up a common display scale, make sure that the limit covers the range of possible data in each panel.

If you use limits, and if there is data point(s) outside the range of the limits, those data points are dropped.

In your example data,  

y <- c(3,2.3,3.1,16,16.5,20)
16, 16.5, 20 are dropped if you set up ylim=c(0,8)

 

This is equivalent to:

qplot(x,y,data=d,geom="boxplot") + scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,8))

 

 

If you don’t want to drop the data but just zoom in the area, use coord_carterian instead (see the difference in output).

qplot(x,y,data=d,geom="boxplot") + coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0,8))
